transcript.content: Hello, welcome to the clinic. What brings you in to see me today?

Well, I came because my husband’s sister has been working this family business so she can get control of the money and push me out of decisions. And she’s always been like that, always needing to be in charge of everything. Like when we were supposed to do the landscaping for the church last spring—or wait, was it fall? I think it was fall because the leaves were everywhere and I had to rake my whole front yard twice. I have this big oak tree that just drops leaves for months, it feels like. My neighbor, he has a gas leaf blower, but he never offers to let me borrow it. Some people are just selfish like that, they just watch you struggle. But anyway, with my sister-in-law, no matter how folks try to smooth it over and tell me I'm making a big deal out of nothing, I know what I’ve been seeing for more than a year now. I'm not blind to what's going on.
Do you think your sister-in-law's actions are targeted specifically at you?

Oh, absolutely it's just at me. Like I was saying a minute ago, she wants control of the money and she wants *me* specifically pushed out of all the family decisions. It's been going on for over a year now, clear as day. And folks try to smooth it over, they really do, saying she's just being "helpful" with the accounts and that I shouldn't take it personal. 

Accounts... you know, that reminds me, I went to the bank on Tuesday to cash a check, and the teller there—the one with the curly red hair, I think her name is Brenda—she took forever. Just chatting away with the person in front of me about some dog rescue. I mean, I like dogs, don't get me wrong. We had a terrier mix when I was a teenager, Buster. He used to dig holes all along the fence line looking for moles. Moles can really ruin a good yard, they just tear up the roots from underneath. My dad used to get so mad he'd sit out there with a lawn chair just waiting for the dirt to move... 

But anyway, what were you asking? Oh, right, my husband's sister. Yeah, no matter what anyone says to make it sound nice or smooth it over, I know what I've been seeing this whole time. She's plotting to get me out of the picture.
Do you think your sister-in-law would be plotting against you if you weren't part of the family business?

Well, I don't know. I guess I haven't really thought about if she'd still be doing it if the business wasn't there. I mean, I don't even work a regular job right now anyway, so the family business is just kind of... there. The last time I had a real punch-the-clock kind of job was years ago at this diner off Highway 9. 

The owner there, he was always yelling about the price of eggs. Eggs used to be so cheap back then, you know? Now you go to the grocery store and a dozen costs you an arm and a leg. I was at the store just yesterday looking at the prices, and this lady in front of me in the checkout line had a whole cart full of nothing but diet soda and cat food. Just cans and cans of it. Makes you wonder how many cats a person really needs. I think more than two is pushing it. My aunt had five cats when I was growing up and her house always smelled like ammonia, no matter how much she opened the windows. She used to buy those little pine tree air fresheners, the kind you hang in your car, and just tape them to the baseboards... 

But anyway, what were you asking? Oh, if she'd still be after me without the business. I really couldn't tell you. Maybe she'd find another reason to be hateful, but the business is what she's using to do it right now.
Do you think your sister-in-law's actions are actually happening, or is it just a feeling you have about her?

Oh, it's actually happening. It's not just some feeling I have. I know what I've been seeing for more than a year now, clear as day. She's working this family business just so she can get control of the money and push me out of all the decisions. And folks try to smooth it over, they really do, but I'm not stupid. 

Speaking of stupid, I felt so silly the other day. I was at the hardware store—the one over on Elm Street, not the big chain one out by the highway—and I couldn't for the life of me remember what size screws I needed for this loose hinge on the back door. The door just kind of sags, you know? It catches on the frame every time you try to close it. My husband says it's just the house settling, but we've lived there fifteen years. How much settling can a house do? You'd think it would be done by now. When I was a kid, we lived in this old farmhouse and the floors were so slanted you could put a marble on one side of the kitchen and watch it roll all the way to the stove. My brother Tommy used to do that for hours when it rained. He ended up joining the Navy, you know. Sent me a postcard from Italy once with this beautiful picture of a fountain...

Wait, what was I saying? Oh, right, my sister-in-law. Yeah, no, it's real. I know what I've been seeing for over a year. She's trying to push me out, and no matter how much people try to tell me I'm imagining things, I know I'm not.
Do you think your sister-in-law would be trying to push you out if you weren't paying attention to her actions?

I mean... I don't really know. Would she still do it if I just ignored her? I haven't really thought about it like that. I guess if you don't pay attention to something, it doesn't just stop happening, right? Like... like weeds. You know, if you stop paying attention to your flowerbeds, the weeds just take over anyway. I was out in the front yard yesterday trying to pull up all these dandelions. They just pop up out of nowhere. You think you got the whole root, but if you leave even a little tiny piece in the dirt, it just grows right back. My neighbor, Mr. Henderson, he uses this chemical spray on his lawn, and it smells just awful. I told him he's going to poison the neighborhood stray cats, but he doesn't listen. He's always been stubborn, ever since he retired from the post office. He used to wear those little blue shorts on his route even when it was freezing out in November... 

Wait, what did you ask me? Oh, about ignoring my sister-in-law. I really couldn't say. I just know what she's doing right now, whether I'm watching her or not.
Do you think it's possible that your sister-in-law's actions might not be intended to harm or push you out?

No, I don't think that's possible. I mean, I know what I've been seeing for more than a year now, clear as day. She's working this family business specifically so she can get control of the money and push me out of the decisions. And folks try to smooth it over, they really do. My husband is always trying to smooth things over. 

He’s just like his mother that way. She used to try and smooth everything over with food. If there was an argument, suddenly there was a fresh batch of oatmeal raisin cookies on the counter. I don't even like oatmeal raisin, to be honest. It's like a trick, you know? You think it's chocolate chip, and then you bite into it and it's a raisin. It just ruins your whole afternoon. I tried making them with dried cranberries once instead, just to see if it was any better. I got those big bags of cranberries on sale after Christmas. They put all the holiday baking stuff on clearance, usually like fifty percent off. I always stock up on vanilla extract then, because the good kind—the pure vanilla, not the imitation stuff—is so expensive... 

Wait, what were you asking me? Oh, about her not meaning any harm. No, no. I came here because of what she's doing. She wants me out, and no matter how much folks try to tell me she doesn't mean it that way, I know exactly what I've been seeing.
Can you think of any situation where you might change your mind about your sister-in-law's intentions?

Change my mind? No, I don't see how I could. I mean, I came here because of this whole situation with my husband's sister. She's been working the family business just so she can get control of the money and push me out of the decisions. And no matter how folks try to smooth it over, I know what I've been seeing for more than a year now. 

Speaking of a year, it's been exactly a year since we had that big ice storm. Do you remember that? The power was out for three whole days. We had to dig all the extra blankets out of the cedar chest in the attic. That chest belonged to my grandmother, you know. She brought it all the way from Pennsylvania when she moved down here in the fifties. It still smells like cedar inside, even after all this time. I keep meaning to polish the brass handles on it, but I never seem to get around to it. There's always something else that needs doing around the house. Like the gutters. They're completely full of leaves right now from the oak tree in the front yard. The squirrels just make a terrible mess up there. I saw one the other day carrying a whole slice of pizza up the trunk. Where do they even get pizza? Probably from the college kids down the street. They leave their trash cans open all the time...

Wait, what was the question? Oh, changing my mind. No, I wouldn't change my mind. I know what she's doing. I've been seeing it for over a year, and nobody can tell me different.
Do you think you've done anything to cause your sister-in-law to act this way towards you?

Me? No, I haven't done a single thing to cause it. I've always been perfectly civil to her. I even bought her a really nice blouse for her birthday last year. I got it at JCPenney, right before they closed the one over at our mall. It's a real shame about that mall. Used to be you could go down there on a Tuesday afternoon and it was just bustling with people. Now it's mostly empty storefronts and teenagers doing those weird little dances for their phones. I saw a group of them right in front of the Auntie Anne's pretzel place last time I was there. I do love those pretzels, though. The cinnamon sugar ones are the best, but only if they're fresh out of the oven. If they sit under those heat lamps too long, they get tough as shoe leather. My Uncle Pete used to actually chew on pieces of rawhide when he was trying to quit smoking his pipe. Said it helped keep his mouth busy, but it completely ruined his front teeth. The dentist told him he was wearing the enamel right down to the nerve... 

Wait, what did you ask me? Oh, if I did something to make her act this way. No, absolutely not. Like I said, I've been nothing but nice to her. She just wants me out of the picture.
Do you think your belief about your sister-in-law's intentions would change if she were to do something unexpectedly kind for you?

Unexpectedly kind? No, I don't think that would change a thing. I know exactly what she's up to. I came here because my husband’s sister has been working this family business just so she can get control of the money and push me out of all the decisions. And no matter how folks try to smooth it over, I know what I’ve been seeing for more than a year now. An act of kindness would just be a front.

Speaking of fronts, it reminds me of that cold front that came through last week. My joints ached for two days before it even started raining. My neighbor, Mrs. Higgins, she swears by this turmeric paste she makes herself for joint pain. She mixes it with black pepper and coconut oil. It stains her fingers completely yellow, though. She looks like she’s been eating mustard with her bare hands. I tried to grow my own turmeric once, but it just rotted in the pot. I think I watered it too much. I'm terrible with houseplants. Even my spider plant died, and they say those are impossible to kill. The only thing that survives in my house is that plastic fern my daughter left behind when she moved out...

Wait, what was the question? Oh, if she did something kind. No, it wouldn't change anything. I've seen her true colors for over a year now. She wants me out, plain and simple.
Do you think there's any evidence that could ever prove your sister-in-law is not trying to push you out?

Evidence? No, there's no evidence that could prove that, because I know what's real. Like I said, I came here because my husband's sister has been working the family business just so she can get control of the money and push me out of the decisions. And no matter how folks try to smooth it over, I know what I've been seeing for more than a year now. You can't just unsee something like that. 

It's like when you see a stain on the carpet, you know? Once you notice it, your eye just goes right to it every time you walk in the room. We have this awful coffee stain right in the middle of the living room rug. My husband spilled it during the Super Bowl three years ago. I've tried everything to get it out—club soda, vinegar, that expensive foam stuff from the hardware store. Nothing works. The hardware store down on Main Street actually has a really good cleaning aisle, though. The man who runs it, Mr. Henderson, he's been there forever. He always gives my dog a little milk bone when we walk by. It's a shame dogs can't eat chocolate, though. I made a chocolate cake from scratch last weekend. Used real cocoa powder and everything. It was so rich, I could only eat one slice. I ended up wrapping the rest in tin foil and putting it in the freezer. Tin foil is getting so expensive lately, have you noticed? I bought a roll at the grocery store and nearly fell over when I saw the receipt. It's just aluminum, for heaven's sake...

Wait, what were we talking about? Oh, evidence about my sister-in-law. No, there's no evidence that would change my mind. I know what she's doing. I've seen it for a year, and I'm not crazy.
Do you think it's possible that someone else, who doesn't know your sister-in-law, would see her actions as harmless?

Someone else? I suppose a stranger might think she's just being helpful, but they don't know her like I do. They haven't seen how she's been working this family business, inching her way in just so she can get control of the money and push me completely out of the decisions. People try to smooth it over, tell me I'm reading into things, but I know what I've been seeing for more than a year now. You can't fool me. 

Speaking of strangers, there was this man at the grocery store yesterday who asked me to help him pick out a cantaloupe. He said he never knows how to tell if they're ripe. I told him you have to smell the stem end, and it should yield just a little bit when you press it. My grandfather taught me that. He used to grow the most massive cantaloupes in his garden out back. He had this whole patch dedicated just to melons. Watermelons, too. But the raccoons always got to the watermelons before we could. Raccoons are so clever with those little hands of theirs. I saw a video on the news where a raccoon actually unlatched a cooler at a campsite and stole a whole package of hot dogs. Just opened it right up like a person! I haven't been camping since my kids were little. We went up to the lake and it rained the entire weekend. We just sat in the tent playing Go Fish and eating slightly damp graham crackers...

Wait, what did you ask me? Oh, if someone else would think she's harmless. Well, maybe they would at first glance, but they'd be wrong. I know what she's really doing with the business and the money, and no stranger is going to convince me otherwise.
Is there anything that could happen in the future that would make you change your mind about your sister-in-law's intentions?

Change my mind in the future? No, I don't see how. I mean, I've been watching my husband's sister work this family business for well over a year now. It’s obvious she’s just trying to get total control of the money and push me completely out of the picture when it comes to any decisions. Everybody else keeps trying to smooth it over and make excuses for her, but I know exactly what I've been seeing. 

Speaking of the future, though, I just bought my new calendar for next year at the mall. I always get the ones with those Thomas Kinkade paintings. You know, the little stone cottages with the glowing windows? They just look so cozy. I’d love to live in a house like that, maybe out in the woods somewhere, just away from all the traffic and noise. Although, the bugs out in the woods can be just terrible in the summer. Last time I went out to a cabin, I got bit by a horsefly the size of a quarter. My arm swelled up like a water balloon. I had to make a paste out of baking soda and water to get the stinging to stop. Baking soda is really a miracle worker, you know. I use it to scrub my kitchen sink, too. You just sprinkle it on with a little lemon juice and it fizzes up and makes the stainless steel shine like it's brand new. Lemons are getting so expensive, though. I paid almost a dollar for one single lemon the other day...

Wait, what were we talking about? Oh, the future. Right. No, nothing's going to happen to make me change my mind about her. I know what she's doing with the business, and I'm not going to let anyone tell me different.
Is there anything your sister-in-law could do or say that would make you question your belief about her intentions?

What could she do or say? Honestly, no, there isn't anything she could say to me. I mean, I've told you already, I came here because my husband’s sister has been working this family business just so she can get control of the money and push me out of decisions. And no matter how folks try to smooth it over, I know what I’ve been seeing for more than a year now. She could swear up and down, but words are just words, you know? 

Like those people who call on the phone and say you've won a cruise. You haven't won a cruise, they just want your credit card number. I had a man call me last Tuesday during my favorite soap opera. He had this really thick accent and said I won an all-expenses-paid trip to the Bahamas. I've never even been to the Bahamas. I don't really like the beach, to be honest. The sand gets everywhere. You find it in your shoes for weeks afterward. I prefer the mountains. My uncle had a cabin up in the Blue Ridge Mountains when I was growing up. We used to go pick blackberries in the summer. You had to wear long sleeves, though, because the thorns would just tear your arms up. And the chiggers! Oh, the chiggers were awful. If you didn't put clear nail polish on the bites, they'd itch for a month. I still buy that same brand of clear nail polish, actually. Sally Hansen. They sell it at the drugstore on the corner. The pharmacist there is so nice. He always asks about my husband's sciatica...

Wait, what did you ask me? Oh, about her saying something to change my mind. Right. No, she couldn't say anything. I know exactly what she's doing with the business, and I'm not blind to it, no matter what anyone else thinks.
Do you think you've done anything that might have contributed to the tension between you and your sister-in-law?

Me? Contribute to the tension? I haven't done a single thing wrong. I've just been sitting back watching my husband's sister try to take over the family business and the money, inching me out of everything. I'm just the one who finally noticed what's been going on for the last year. 

Speaking of noticing things, I noticed the other day that the streetlights on our block are turning on way too early. It wasn't even five o'clock and they were blazing away. It just seems like such a waste of electricity. My father used to follow us around the house turning off lights. He'd say, "Do you think I own the electric company?" He worked for the city, actually, driving one of those street sweepers. I always thought that looked like a fun job, just driving slowly down the street, brushing up all the leaves. The leaves this year have been terrible. I spent three hours raking the front yard on Sunday, and by Monday morning, it looked like I hadn't done a thing. The wind just blows them right back over from the Johnson's yard. They have this massive oak tree that drops acorns everywhere. Stepping on an acorn in bare feet is worse than stepping on a Lego, I swear. My grandson left his Legos all over the living room floor last Thanksgiving and I nearly broke my toe...

Wait, what was the question? Oh, if I did something to cause the tension. No, absolutely not. I haven't done anything but see the truth about what she's doing with the business.
Do you think your belief about your sister-in-law's intentions could be considered an exaggeration by someone who doesn't know her?

An exaggeration? By someone who doesn't know her? Well, maybe they might think that, if they just walked in off the street. But I'm the one living it. Like I've been saying, my husband's sister is working that family business for one reason—to get her hands on all the money and completely push me out of any decisions. It's been going on for over a year, and folks can try to smooth it over all they want, but I know what I'm seeing. 

Speaking of seeing things, I went to get my eyes checked last week at that new place by the grocery store. The optometrist there was so young, he looked like he was barely out of high school. He had these bright red glasses frames. I don't know if I could pull off red glasses. I usually stick to the wire ones, they just blend in better. My mother wore those thick plastic ones in the seventies, the ones that took up half her face. She used to put them on a chain around her neck so she wouldn't lose them, but they'd always swing forward and dunk right into her coffee cup when she leaned over the table. She loved her coffee, black as tar. She'd buy those big metal tins of Folgers. I use those old coffee tins to hold my sewing supplies now. You can fit so many spools of thread in them, and they stack up nicely in the closet. I have so much thread, but I can never find the right color when I actually need to fix a hem...

Wait, what were you asking me? Oh, about people thinking I'm exaggerating. Right. Well, they don't know her. I know exactly what she's doing to push me out of the business, and it's no exaggeration at all.
Do you think your belief about your sister-in-law's intentions could change if you discovered she was acting in your best interest?

If I discovered she was acting in my best interest? Well, that's just the thing, isn't it? That's a big "if." Because I've told you, I came here because my husband’s sister has been working this family business just so she can get control of the money and push me out of decisions. I've been seeing it for over a year now, and no matter how folks try to smooth it over, I know what's happening. So her acting in my best interest... that just doesn't make any sense. 

Speaking of things that don't make sense, did you know they changed the layout at the grocery store again? I went in for milk yesterday, and they moved the dairy section all the way to the other side of the store. Why do they do that? You get used to a routine, you know exactly where the butter is, and then bam, it's next to the frozen pizzas. I ended up wandering down the baking aisle and bought three bags of chocolate chips on sale. I don't even bake cookies that often anymore. My kids used to eat them up as fast as I could pull them out of the oven, but now it's just me and my husband. He shouldn't be eating sweets anyway, his doctor told him his blood sugar is creeping up. He loves those little hard candies, though, the butterscotch ones wrapped in the yellow cellophane. My grandmother used to keep those in her purse. They were always covered in lint by the time she gave you one, but you ate it anyway because you didn't want to be rude. She had this huge, heavy leather purse that smelled like peppermint and old receipts. I carry a small crossbody bag now, it's so much easier on my shoulder...

Wait, what did you ask me? Oh, about her acting in my best interest. Right. Well, like I said, I know what I've been seeing for a year. She's just trying to push me out and get the money, so I don't see how she could be doing anything for my own good.
Do you think it's possible that your interpretation of your sister-in-law's actions might be incorrect?

Incorrect? Me, incorrect about this? No, I don't think so. I mean, I'm the one who's been watching it happen. I came here because my husband’s sister has been working this family business just so she can get control of the money and push me out of all the decisions. I've been seeing it plain as day for more than a year now, and no matter how folks try to smooth it over or tell me I'm wrong, I know what I've been seeing. 

Speaking of seeing things wrong, did you see the weather report this morning? The weatherman said it was supposed to be bright and sunny all day, not a cloud in the sky. I hung all my sheets out on the clothesline because there's nothing better than sheets dried in the sun, they just smell so crisp. But then around noon, these huge dark clouds rolled in out of nowhere. I had to sprint out back and pull everything down before the rain started. I tripped over the garden hose trying to get to the basket. We really need to get one of those reels for the hose, it's always just coiled up in a messy pile by the spigot. My neighbor, Mr. Henderson, has this fancy automatic one that rolls itself back up. He's always out there watering his prize-winning tomatoes. He brought us a basket of them last August, big juicy red ones. I made a huge batch of marinara sauce and froze it in those plastic containers you get from takeout restaurants. I have a whole cabinet full of those containers, I can never bring myself to throw them away. But then you can never find the right lid...

Wait, what were we talking about? Oh, if I could be incorrect. No, no. Like I said, I know what she's doing. She's trying to push me out and get the money, and no one can tell me otherwise.
Do you think it's possible that your sister-in-law is not plotting against you and everything you've been thinking is just a misunderstanding?

A misunderstanding? You think I'm just misunderstanding her? No, absolutely not. I mean, I've told you why I'm here. My husband's sister has been working in this family business for one reason—to get control of the money and completely push me out of any decisions. I've been watching it happen for more than a year, and folks can try to smooth it over all they want, but I know what I'm seeing. 

Speaking of misunderstandings, though, I had the strangest misunderstanding with the mail carrier on Tuesday. He left this huge, heavy cardboard box on my front step, and when I went to look at the label, it wasn't even for me. It was for a family three streets over! I think it was dog food or something. People order the heaviest things through the mail these days, it's crazy. My cousin used to have this big, goofy golden retriever that ate like a horse, and he’d buy those fifty-pound bags from the feed store. That dog, oh, what was his name... Barnaby! Barnaby used to dig these massive holes in the backyard. My cousin's wife was so mad because she was trying to grow prize-winning hydrangeas. You have to put pennies in the soil to make the flowers turn blue, did you know that? Or maybe it's coffee grounds. I tried growing a fern in my living room last month, but the leaves all turned brown and crispy. I think I put it too close to the radiator. The heat in our house is so unpredictable, one minute you're freezing and the next you're sweating through your sweater...

Wait, what was the question? Oh, if I was just misunderstanding her. Right. Well, no. Like I said, I know exactly what I've been seeing for over a year now. She wants the money and she wants me out of the decisions. There's no misunderstanding about it.
Is there anything that could make you doubt your belief about your sister-in-law's intentions?

Doubt it? You keep asking me these questions like I'm making it all up. Like I keep telling you, I know exactly why I'm here. My husband’s sister is working the family business for one reason—to get control of all the money and push me completely out of the decisions. Folks are always trying to smooth it over, but I've been watching it happen for more than a year now, and I know what I've been seeing. So no, I don't doubt it for a second.

Speaking of doubting things, though, I really doubted that new stain remover I bought at the hardware store on Tuesday. I usually don't buy those miracle cleaners, but I saw a commercial for it and thought, why not? My husband spilled black coffee all over his favorite recliner. It's this awful brown corduroy chair he's had since before we even got married. I've tried to throw it out at least three times, but he always catches me. Once I even dragged it all the way out to the curb, but the garbage men wouldn't take it because I didn't have the right bulky item sticker. You have to call city hall for those stickers now, and you sit on hold for twenty minutes just to talk to a real person. The hold music is always that same fuzzy elevator music, it just loops over and over. I put the phone on speaker and started folding laundry, but then the cat jumped on the table and knocked over my good lamp. It didn't break the bulb, thank goodness, but the shade is all dented now. I tried popping it back out with a wooden spoon, but you can still see the crease when the light is turned on... 

I'm sorry, what were you asking? Oh, if anything would make me doubt it. No. Like I said, I know what I'm seeing with her and the business. She wants the money and she wants me out, and there's no doubting that.

My neighbor, Mr. Henderson, has this fancy automatic one that rolls itself back up. He's always out there watering his prize-winning tomatoes. He brought us a basket of them last August, big juicy red ones. I made a huge batch of marinara sauce and froze it in those plastic containers you get from takeout restaurants. I have a whole cabinet full of those containers, I can never bring myself to throw them away. But then you can never find the right lid...

Wait, what were we talking about? Oh, if I could be incorrect. No, no. Like I said, I know what she's doing. She's trying to push me out and get the money, and no one can tell me otherwise.

doctor.intent: Determine if the patient's beliefs are delusional
doctor.question: Do you think it's possible that your sister-in-law is not plotting against you and everything you've been thinking is just a misunderstanding?

target_item.name: Delusions
target_item.manifestation: I came because my husband’s sister has been working this family business so she can get control of the money and push me out of decisions, and no matter how folks try to smooth it over, I know what I’ve been seeing for more than a year now.
target_item.reason: The doctor is again challenging the patient's belief, asking if it could be a misunderstanding, which directly assesses the fixed nature of the delusional belief.

patient.answer:
A misunderstanding? You think I'm just misunderstanding her? No, absolutely not. I mean, I've told you why I'm here. My husband's sister has been working in this family business for one reason—to get control of the money and completely push me out of any decisions. I've been watching it happen for more than a year, and folks can try to smooth it over all they want, but I know what I'm seeing. 

Speaking of misunderstandings, though, I had the strangest misunderstanding with the mail carrier on Tuesday. He left this huge, heavy cardboard box on my front step, and when I went to look at the label, it wasn't even for me. It was for a family three streets over! I think it was dog food or something. People order the heaviest things through the mail these days, it's crazy. My cousin used to have this big, goofy golden retriever that ate like a horse, and he’d buy those fifty-pound bags from the feed store. That dog, oh, what was his name... Barnaby! Barnaby used to dig these massive holes in the backyard. My cousin's wife was so mad because she was trying to grow prize-winning hydrangeas. You have to put pennies in the soil to make the flowers turn blue, did you know that? Or maybe it's coffee grounds. I tried growing a fern in my living room last month, but the leaves all turned brown and crispy. I think I put it too close to the radiator. The heat in our house is so unpredictable, one minute you're freezing and the next you're sweating through your sweater...

Wait, what was the question? Oh, if I was just misunderstanding her. Right. Well, no. Like I said, I know exactly what I've been seeing for over a year now. She wants the money and she wants me out of the decisions. There's no misunderstanding about it.

doctor.intent: Determine if the patient's beliefs are fixed and unchangeable
doctor.question: Is there anything that could make you doubt your belief about your sister-in-law's intentions?

target_item.name: Delusions
target_item.manifestation: I came because my husband’s sister has been working this family business so she can get control of the money and push me out of decisions, and no matter how folks try to smooth it over, I know what I’ve been seeing for more than a year now.
target_item.reason: The doctor is asking if anything could make the patient doubt her beliefs, which directly assesses the fixity of the delusion.

patient.answer:
Doubt it? You keep asking me these questions like I'm making it all up. Like I keep telling you, I know exactly why I'm here. My husband’s sister is working the family business for one reason—to get control of all the money and push me completely out of the decisions. Folks are always trying to smooth it over, but I've been watching it happen for more than a year now, and I know what I've been seeing. So no, I don't doubt it for a second.

Speaking of doubting things, though, I really doubted that new stain remover I bought at the hardware store on Tuesday. I usually don't buy those miracle cleaners, but I saw a commercial for it and thought, why not? My husband spilled black coffee all over his favorite recliner. It's this awful brown corduroy chair he's had since before we even got married. I've tried to throw it out at least three times, but he always catches me. Once I even dragged it all the way out to the curb, but the garbage men wouldn't take it because I didn't have the right bulky item sticker. You have to call city hall for those stickers now, and you sit on hold for twenty minutes just to talk to a real person. The hold music is always that same fuzzy elevator music, it just loops over and over. I put the phone on speaker and started folding laundry, but then the cat jumped on the table and knocked over my good lamp. It didn't break the bulb, thank goodness, but the shade is all dented now. I tried popping it back out with a wooden spoon, but you can still see the crease when the light is turned on... 

I'm sorry, what were you asking? Oh, if anything would make me doubt it. No. Like I said, I know what I'm seeing with her and the business. She wants the money and she wants me out, and there's no doubting that.
